2	
3	Written 2026-11-20 from measurements on caliper `main` (c633fbc6 plus docs). Nothing here is merged work; it is evidence and a map.
4	
5	## What we use
6	
7	- **`tsrs`** is `oxc-project/tsrs` (Apache-2.0), a Rust port of the TypeScript 7.1 checker. It is upstream, not ours. We pin the crates exactly: `tsrs_api`, `tsrs_vfs`, `tsrs_core` `=0.24.0` (TypeScript commit `3e9236361fa9`, `typescript@7.1.0-beta`). Pin changes are deliberate, never through dependabot (ADR 0026).
8	- **Linked, not spawned** (ADR 0026, trail 369): we link the crates and ask `tsrs_api::Session` in process. Measured then: the same recorded Chakra answer, 3,776 requests, took 141 ms in process against 367 ms over a pipe.
9	- **How we ask:** `crates/semantic/src/checker.rs` creates a `Session` on a thread of its own with a 512 MiB stack (a type 2,000 deep overflows a default stack and aborts the process). `Session::new(SessionOptions::new(cwd, bundled::lib_path(), fs, false))`. TypeScript's lib files (`lib.dom.d.ts`, ES libs) are bundled inside `tsrs_vfs`, not read from the project. `@types/react` and csstype are read from the project's `node_modules`.
10	- **`tsrs_api` is a port of TypeScript's JSON API server** (`session.go`, `proto.go`). Every request is a JSON method plus params; every answer is `Response::Json(String)`. Our `crates/semantic/src/rpc.rs` builds params as `serde_json::Value`, serializes them, the handler parses them again, answers as text, and we parse that. Batching exists (`batchRequests`, `rpc.batch(..)` in `declared.rs`).
11	- **Who calls it:** `component.rs` (per component: props, `composes` walk, `leave_to_layers`), `convert.rs` (the type converter, memoized by type id within one snapshot), `declared.rs` (declarations by name, batched), `instantiate.rs` (generic component instantiation through a generated probe file; it calls `getSemanticDiagnostics` on that file), `lib.rs` (scheduler, prefetch, kept answers). Docs: `docs/type-checker-integration.md`, ADR 0022, ADR 0026, `docs/gate-measurements.md`.
12	
13	## Measurements (release builds, machine at load 11 to 22; trust ratios and counts, not absolute times)
14	
15	Cold default run (checker on, `--load-dependencies`, `--no-cache`), shadcn `apps/v4`, 2.06 s wall, 6.6 CPU-seconds:
16	
17	| Phase (traced) | Span |
18	| --- | --- |
19	| structural parse and module resolution (about 20,000 resolver calls for 1,385 files) | 0 to 312 ms |
20	| unexplained before the first checker answer | 312 to 565 ms |
21	| about 1,800 component answers (about 0.6 ms each, 32,251 requests, mean 17.9 per component) | 565 to 1690 ms |
22	| merge and serialization of 4.7 MB JSON | to about 2 s |
23	
24	Busy CPU by subsystem (profiling build, sampled from launch): allocation and copying 24.8%, JSON codec (checker IPC) 21.4%, `tsrs` checker work 14.5%, files and VFS 10.1%, tsrs parse, bind and symbols 6.9%, caliper core 4.6%, other 16.6%. About 60% of thread samples are idle waits.
25	
26	Spike worker (instrumented `rpc.rs`, shadcn cold run):
27	- About 33.7k top-level requests plus 17.9k sub-requests inside 4,060 `batchRequests`. Top-level counts: `getTypeOfSymbol` 3,602, `getTypesOfType` 3,146, `getParametersOfSignature` 3,089, `getSignaturesOfType` 3,086, `getTypesOfSymbols` 2,726, `getBaseTypes` 2,433, `getPropertiesOfType` 1,708, `getAliasedSymbol` 1,416, `getSymbolOfType` 1,375, `typeToString` 1,310.
28	- Codec at least about 450 ms (ours: encode 11, RawValue validate 116, decode 182; tsrs side lower bound: decode 17, marshal 120). Handler time 1,776 ms in all; of that `getSemanticDiagnostics` (one call) 797 ms, `getPropertiesOfType` 546 ms, `parseConfigFile` 48 ms. Payload: 11 MB of requests, 212 MB of responses.
29	- Direct typed calls are possible without forking, but only by going around `tsrs_api`'s private handlers and rewriting our query layer against `tsrs_checker::Checker` (`get_properties_of_type_exported`, `get_type_of_symbol_exported`, `get_signatures_of_type_exported`, `get_base_types`, ...; JSDoc through `tsrs_ls`). Estimate 1.5 to 3 weeks. Risks: the handler does state-changing work (`MappedType::resolve_components`, MembersResolved fix-up) whose omission can change results; `catch_unwind` is lost; the `*_exported` API is unstable across pins; a `P<..>` outliving its snapshot is a dangling pointer.
30	
31	Request profile by corpus (instrumented release build; load 22 to 30 so times are secondary; counts exact; caller attribution sampled 1 in 4, scaled):
32	
33	| corpus | requests | batches | sub-requests in batches | identical repeats (same method and params) |
34	| --- | --: | --: | --: | --- |
35	| shadcn | 33.2k | 4,043 | 17.9k | getBaseTypes 1,718 of 2,433 |
36	| chakra | 58.9k | 12,311 | 777k (743k are `isReadonlySymbol`) | getAliasTypeArgumentsOfType 5,714 of 8,048; typeToString 3,646 of 7,375; getTypeArguments 2,952 of 5,710; getBaseTypes 3,600 of 4,881; getTypesOfSymbols 4,069 of 6,413; batchRequests 8,170 of 12,311 |
37	| mantine | 27.7k | 7,970 | 65k | getBaseTypes 1,810 of 2,232; getTypesOfSymbols 2,109 of 4,594; batchRequests 3,723 of 7,970 |
38	
39	- By time: shadcn `getPropertiesOfType` 777 ms, `getSemanticDiagnostics` 580 (one call), `getTypeOfSymbol` 385, `batchRequests` 371. Chakra `batchRequests` 3.6 s (261 MB of responses), `getTypesOfSymbols` 1.9 s, `getAliasTypeArgumentsOfType` 1.3 s, `getTypesOfType` 0.86 s. Mantine `batchRequests` 776 ms, `getSemanticDiagnostics` 382.
40	- By bytes: shadcn `getPropertiesOfType` 193 MB (113 KB per call, 684 of 1,708 are repeats); chakra `batchRequests` 261 MB and `getPropertiesOfType` 194 MB in 620 calls.
41	- Callers: `convert.rs` `Converter::object` (via `uncached` and `convert`) issues `batchRequests`, `getParametersOfSignature`, `getReturnTypeOfSignature`, `getSignaturesOfType`, `getTypesOfSymbols` (22 to 38% of requests). `Converter::fields` (about line 1751) issues the `isReadonlySymbol` batch plus `types_of_symbols` for every property of every object type. `Converter::parts` (`members_text`, `type_arguments_text`, about line 1080) issues `getTypesOfType`, `getTypeArguments`. `Converter::printed` issues `typeToString`. `component.rs` `props_of_type` issues `getPropertiesOfType`, `getBaseTypes`, `getAliasTypeArgumentsOfType`, `getTargetOfType` (about 7.1k of shadcn's 33k). `declared.rs` lines 109 and 218 issue batches. `answer_file` inlines `aliased_symbol`, `type_of_symbol`, `signatures`, `parameters` (about 5.5 requests per component).
42	- Repeats: a per-run memo keyed by (method, params) on `getBaseTypes`, `getAliasTypeArgumentsOfType`, `getTypeArguments`, `typeToString`, `getTypesOfSymbols` would remove most of them; call sites `convert.rs` lines 873, 912, 916, 1230, 1584, 1603, 1617, 1658. The converter's type-id memo evidently does not catch them. Not checked: whether the repeats come from the same component or different ones.
43	- Back-to-back same-method runs: `batchRequests` after `batchRequests` (581 in shadcn, 3.9k in chakra), `typeToString` twice (1.9k in chakra), `getTypeArguments`, `getAliasTypeArgumentsOfType`, `getTypesOfType` twice: per-item loops in `parts`, `printed`, `type_arguments_of` that could go through `rpc.batch`. Per signature: `getSignaturesOfType`, then `getParametersOfSignature`, then `getTypeOfSymbol` per parameter, then `getReturnTypeOfSignature`. In shadcn 1,171 batches have size 1 or 2.
44	
45	Floor: a two-component project costs 30 ms structural, 40 ms with the checker, so lib and React type loading is not the cold-start cost.
46	
47	## What to dig into (in this order)
48	
49	0. **Chakra's `isReadonlySymbol` (743k sub-requests, most of its 12.3k batches and 261 MB, `batchRequests` 3.6 s of a 5 to 7 s run).** `Converter::fields` asks readonly-ness for every property of every object type it converts. Find out whether the property flags already in the `getPropertiesOfType` or `getTypesOfSymbols` answer carry it (then drop the calls), or whether it can be asked only for properties that are shown or converted for a visible row (not for names left in a collapsed layer or in nested types nobody reads). Likely the largest single saving on the heaviest corpus.
50	0b. **A per-run memo keyed by (method, params)** for the repeated calls listed in the request profile (`getBaseTypes` 70 to 81% repeats; on Chakra roughly 28k of 59k requests are identical repeats). Cheapest change, no upstream dependency; check first whether repeats are cross-component (a shared cache wins) or same-component (a missing memo in one function).
51	1. **`getSemanticDiagnostics` on the probe file (797 ms, about 45% of handler time).** `instantiate.rs:182` calls it to find which generic instantiations fail. A whole-file check forces every instantiation's evaluation, so some of that work is paid later anyway. Find out how much is avoidable: resolve each probe's type individually and read an error type; check only the probe lines; or skip probes whose arguments are trivial. Measure total wall before and after, not just this call.
52	2. **`getPropertiesOfType` payload (546 ms, most of the 212 MB of responses).** What fields do we use out of each answer, and what does the handler send? Candidate: a leaner response or a field mask (upstream), or fewer calls (we ask 1,708 times plus 1,787 inside batches).
53	3. **Request count per component (mean 17.9).** Which converter functions issue them (`convert.rs` `composes`, `base_layers`, `named_bases`), which repeat for the same type id across components (React types such as `HTMLAttributes` and its bases), and which loops could use the existing batch. A memo keyed by type id inside one snapshot is the cheapest candidate. A request-profile worker may have a by-method table.
54	4. **An upstream typed result path.** Draft an issue for `oxc-project/tsrs`: a `Response` variant (or sink) that returns the structured value instead of JSON text, plus a smaller `getPropertiesOfType`. Attach the numbers above. Do not open it; the owner sends it.
55	5. **Hot spots inside `tsrs` for an upstream patch** (from top-of-stack samples, unverified against their code): `SymbolMap::insert` and its hash-table rehash (a pre-sized table), `JsonMap::get_index_of` (looks like a linear search), `NodeIndexTable::get_index` in the API encoder, and repeated `stat`, `lstat`, `open`, `SourceFS::source`, `directory_exists` calls (about 120 samples; a per-run stat cache).
56	6. **The unexplained 250 ms before the first answer** (312 to 565 ms): find what runs there (structural second pass, relevance inputs, building targets, program creation).
57	7. **The resolver:** about 20,000 `resolve_dts`, `resolve` and `find_tsconfig` calls for 1,385 files; the same specifiers repeat. A memo per (directory, specifier) is a candidate.
58	
59	## How to measure
60	
61	- Corpora (cloned and installed): `~/.cache/caliper/corpora/repos/{mantine/packages/@mantine/core/src, chakra-ui/packages/react/src, shadcn-ui/apps/v4, ant-design/components, react-spectrum/packages}`. 62	- Run: `target/release/caliper-docgen extract --src <dir> --quiet --no-cache --load-dependencies --json` under `/usr/bin/time -l`. Interleave main against the branch, best of 5 to 7. 63	- Profiling build with symbols: `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_STRIP=none REDACTED cargo build --release -p caliper-docgen --target-dir <scratch>`. `sample caliper-docgen 8 1 -wait -mayDie -f <file>` started before the run attaches from launch (without `-wait` it attaches too late).

Docs: `docs/type-checker-integration.md`, ADR 0022, ADR 0026, `docs/gate-measurements.md`.

Cold default run (checker on, `--load-dependencies`, `--no-cache`), shadcn `apps/v4`, 2.06 s wall, 6.6 CPU-seconds:

| Phase (traced) | Span |
| --- | --- |
| structural parse and module resolution (about 20,000 resolver calls for 1,385 files) | 0 to 312 ms |
| unexplained before the first checker answer | 312 to 565 ms |
| about 1,800 component answers (about 0.6 ms each, 32,251 requests, mean 17.9 per component) | 565 to 1690 ms |
| merge and serialization of 4.7 MB JSON | to about 2 s |

Busy CPU by subsystem (profiling build, sampled from launch): allocation and copying 24.8%, JSON codec (checker IPC) 21.4%, `tsrs` checker work 14.5%, files and VFS 10.1%, tsrs parse, bind and symbols 6.9%, caliper core 4.6%, other 16.6%. About 60% of thread samples are idle waits.

Spike worker (instrumented `rpc.rs`, shadcn cold run):
- About 33.7k top-level requests plus 17.9k sub-requests inside 4,060 `batchRequests`. Top-level counts: `getTypeOfSymbol` 3,602, `getTypesOfType` 3,146, `getParametersOfSignature` 3,089, `getSignaturesOfType` 3,086, `getTypesOfSymbols` 2,726, `getBaseTypes` 2,433, `getPropertiesOfType` 1,708, `getAliasedSymbol` 1,416, `getSymbolOfType` 1,375, `typeToString` 1,310.
- Codec at least about 450 ms (ours: encode 11, RawValue validate 116, decode 182; tsrs side lower bound: decode 17, marshal 120). Handler time 1,776 ms in all; of that `getSemanticDiagnostics` (one call) 797 ms, `getPropertiesOfType` 546 ms, `parseConfigFile` 48 ms. Payload: 11 MB of requests, 212 MB of responses.
- Direct typed calls are possible without forking, but only by going around `tsrs_api`'s private handlers and rewriting our query layer against `tsrs_checker::Checker` (`get_properties_of_type_exported`, `get_type_of_symbol_exported`, `get_signatures_of_type_exported`, `get_base_types`, ...; JSDoc through `tsrs_ls`). State needed: `Session::snapshot_data(id)`, `.get_program(&ProjectID)`, `checker::lease::acquire(program)`, `program.get_type_checker(...)`. `CheckerRegistry::register_*` is `pub(crate)`, so it is all-or-nothing per snapshot. Estimate 1.5 to 3 weeks. Risks: the handler does state-changing work (`MappedType::resolve_components`, MembersResolved fix-up) whose omission can change results; `catch_unwind` is lost; the `*_exported` API is unstable across pins; a `P<..>` outliving its snapshot is a dangling pointer.

Request profile by corpus (instrumented release build; load 22 to 30 so times are secondary; counts exact; caller attribution sampled 1 in 4, scaled):

| corpus | requests | batches | sub-requests in batches | identical repeats (same method and params) |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --- |
| shadcn | 33.2k | 4,043 | 17.9k | getBaseTypes 1,718 of 2,433 |
| chakra | 58.9k | 12,311 | 777k (743k are `isReadonlySymbol`) | getAliasTypeArgumentsOfType 5,714 of 8,048; typeToString 3,646 of 7,375; getTypeArguments 2,952 of 5,710; getBaseTypes 3,600 of 4,881; getTypesOfSymbols 4,069 of 6,413; batchRequests 8,170 of 12,311 |
| mantine | 27.7k | 7,970 | 65k | getBaseTypes 1,810 of 2,232; getTypesOfSymbols 2,109 of 4,594; batchRequests 3,723 of 7,970 |

- By time: shadcn `getPropertiesOfType` 777 ms, `getSemanticDiagnostics` 580 (one call), `getTypeOfSymbol` 385, `batchRequests` 371. Chakra `batchRequests` 3.6 s (261 MB of responses), `getTypesOfSymbols` 1.9 s, `getAliasTypeArgumentsOfType` 1.3 s, `getTypesOfType` 0.86 s. Mantine `batchRequests` 776 ms, `getSemanticDiagnostics` 382.
- By bytes: shadcn `getPropertiesOfType` 193 MB (113 KB per call, 684 of 1,708 are repeats); chakra `batchRequests` 261 MB and `getPropertiesOfType` 194 MB in 620 calls.
- Callers: `convert.rs` `Converter::object` (via `uncached` and `convert`) issues `batchRequests`, `getParametersOfSignature`, `getReturnTypeOfSignature`, `getSignaturesOfType`, `getTypesOfSymbols` (22 to 38% of requests). `Converter::fields` (about line 1751) issues the `isReadonlySymbol` batch plus `types_of_symbols` for every property of every object type. `Converter::parts` (`members_text`, `type_arguments_text`, about line 1080) issues `getTypesOfType`, `getTypeArguments`. `Converter::printed` issues `typeToString`. `component.rs` `props_of_type` issues `getPropertiesOfType`, `getBaseTypes`, `getAliasTypeArgumentsOfType`, `getTargetOfType` (about 7.1k of shadcn's 33k). `declared.rs` lines 109 and 218 issue batches. `answer_file` inlines `aliased_symbol`, `type_of_symbol`, `signatures`, `parameters` (about 5.5 requests per component).
- Repeats: a per-run memo keyed by (method, params) on `getBaseTypes`, `getAliasTypeArgumentsOfType`, `getTypeArguments`, `typeToString`, `getTypesOfSymbols` would remove most of them; call sites `convert.rs` lines 873, 912, 916, 1230, 1584, 1603, 1617, 1658. The converter's type-id memo evidently does not catch them. Not checked: whether the repeats come from the same component or different ones.
- Back-to-back same-method runs: `batchRequests` after `batchRequests` (581 in shadcn, 3.9k in chakra), `typeToString` twice (1.9k in chakra), `getTypeArguments`, `getAliasTypeArgumentsOfType`, `getTypesOfType` twice: per-item loops in `parts`, `printed`, `type_arguments_of` that could go through `rpc.batch`. Per signature: `getSignaturesOfType`, then `getParametersOfSignature`, then `getTypeOfSymbol` per parameter, then `getReturnTypeOfSignature`. In shadcn 1,171 batches have size 1 or 2.

## What to dig into (in this order)

0. **Chakra's `isReadonlySymbol` (743k sub-requests, most of its 12.3k batches and 261 MB, `batchRequests` 3.6 s of a 5 to 7 s run).** `Converter::fields` asks readonly-ness for every property of every object type it converts. Find out whether the property flags already in the `getPropertiesOfType` or `getTypesOfSymbols` answer carry it (then drop the calls), or whether it can be asked only for properties that are shown or converted for a visible row (not for names left in a collapsed layer or in nested types nobody reads). Likely the largest single saving on the heaviest corpus.
0b. **A per-run memo keyed by (method, params)** for the repeated calls listed in the request profile (`getBaseTypes` 70 to 81% repeats; on Chakra roughly 28k of 59k requests are identical repeats). Cheapest change, no upstream dependency; check first whether repeats are cross-component (a shared cache wins) or same-component (a missing memo in one function).
1. **`getSemanticDiagnostics` on the probe file (797 ms, about 45% of handler time).** `instantiate.rs:182` calls it to find which generic instantiations fail. A whole-file check forces every instantiation's evaluation, so some of that work is paid later anyway. Find out how much is avoidable: resolve each probe's type individually and read an error type; check only the probe lines; or skip probes whose arguments are trivial. Measure total wall before and after, not just this call.
2. **`getPropertiesOfType` payload (546 ms, most of the 212 MB of responses).** What fields do we use out of each answer, and what does the handler send? Candidate: a leaner response or a field mask (upstream), or fewer calls (we ask 1,708 times plus 1,787 inside batches).
3. **Request count per component (mean 17.9).** Which converter functions issue them (`convert.rs` `composes`, `base_layers`, `named_bases`), which repeat for the same type id across components (React types such as `HTMLAttributes` and its bases), and which loops could use the existing batch. A memo keyed by type id inside one snapshot is the cheapest candidate. A request-profile worker may have a by-method table.
4. **An upstream typed result path.** Draft an issue for `oxc-project/tsrs`: a `Response` variant (or sink) that returns the structured value instead of JSON text, plus a smaller `getPropertiesOfType`. Attach the numbers above. Do not open it; the owner sends it.
5. **Hot spots inside `tsrs` for an upstream patch** (from top-of-stack samples, unverified against their code): `SymbolMap::insert` and its hash-table rehash (a pre-sized table), `JsonMap::get_index_of` (looks like a linear search), `NodeIndexTable::get_index` in the API encoder, and repeated `stat`, `lstat`, `open`, `SourceFS::source`, `directory_exists` calls (about 120 samples; a per-run stat cache).
6. **The unexplained 250 ms before the first answer** (312 to 565 ms): find what runs there (structural second pass, relevance inputs, building targets, program creation).
7. **The resolver:** about 20,000 `resolve_dts`, `resolve` and `find_tsconfig` calls for 1,385 files; the same specifiers repeat. A memo per (directory, specifier) is a candidate.

- Corpora (cloned and installed): `~/.cache/caliper/corpora/repos/{mantine/packages/@mantine/core/src, chakra-ui/packages/react/src, shadcn-ui/apps/v4, ant-design/components, react-spectrum/packages}`. [workspace]
members = [
    "crates/core",
    "crates/binding",
    "crates/cli",
    "crates/semantic",
]
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.99"
authors = ["caliper-docgen contributors"]
license = "FSL-1.1-MIT"
repository = "https://github.com/orin-dx/caliper"
homepage = "https://orin-dx.com/tools/caliper/"
keywords = ["react", "docgen", "typescript", "oxc", "storybook"]
categories = ["development-tools", "command-line-utilities"]

# "deny" rather than "forbid": a member crate could locally #[allow(unsafe_code)]
# on a real FFI boundary if one ever needs it. One does: crates/semantic/src/heap.rs reads
# mimalloc's committed bytes and the machine's memory (two calls). Otherwise zero `unsafe`
# across crates/core, crates/cli, crates/binding; napi-rs's #[napi] macros generate the FFI
# glue without user-visible unsafe.
[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "deny"
unused_must_use = "deny"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
unwrap_used = "deny"
expect_used = "deny"
panic = "deny"
dbg_macro = "deny"
# Only `main` ends the process, so a command's exit decision stays testable; the one other exit is allowed in place.
exit = "deny"
print_stdout = "deny"
print_stderr = "deny"
map_err_ignore = "deny"
let_underscore_must_use = "deny"
